name: GRAVBALL SHELF OPEN: Municipal Independent League
description: The Shelf Open is the independent municipal cousin of the GRAVBALL CONTINENTAL, played in Tier 1 and Tier 2 districts on repurposed vertical infrastructure using salvaged gravity-assist rail rigs that are frequently malfunctioning, jury-rigged, or running at illegal power draws from the city grid. Teams are neighborhood-organized, self-funded, and governed by the Municipal Gravball Compact — a body that has no formal legal recognition but commands enormous community authority across the Shelf. Augmentation is not regulated but economic reality means most players are unmodified or minimally augmented.
story_hooks: A GRAVBALL CONTINENTAL scout watching a Shelf Open match to find cheap talent realizes the player she's come to poach is being protected by her community from exactly the kind of extraction the scout represents.

The Municipal Gravball Compact's de facto leader is being pressured by a local syndicate to allow betting operations into Shelf Open matches — a change that would bring money but transform the culture of the only thing keeping two rival districts from open conflict.

A city infrastructure official who has been sitting on repair requests for the Shelf Open's power rigs for three years receives an anonymous message: fix it, or the next grid surge gets filmed and broadcast to every feed in GLMZ.
